source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: After testing a guess, decide from the result whether the guess is supported or whether a different reason must be tried.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The empty refill proves that finished ink is the only possible explanation.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The refill still contains ink, but the ink-finished guess is supported because we tested it.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: The refill is empty, so the ink-finished guess is not supported; try another reason.

intelligence.enrichment: A test result is used to judge a guess: if the result matches the guess, the guess is supported; if the result does not match, another possible answer should be considered. The outcome of the test changes the status of the guess, which then determines whether to accept that explanation or search for another one. The learner uses the test result to decide whether the guess is supported or whether another possible answer is needed. The first guess is probably true unless someone gives a different answer.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: The wonderful world of science. The student must decide: After testing a guess, decide from the result whether the guess is supported or whether a different reason must be tried. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
